name: smarthire-ai
description: Smart Hire AI — Electron desktop app and its Next.js licensing backend
_comment_workspaces: SPLIT 2026-09-01: packages/* are listed FIRST so npm links them before the apps that depend on them. smarthire-pricing has no dependencies and no peer dependencies at all — that is what keeps apps/desktop (React 18, Tailwind 3, pinned deliberately; see the version note in the README) able to consume it one day without npm resolving a second React into the tree. ADMIN SPLIT 2026-09-01: apps/* is NOT globbed, so apps/admin had to be added by hand here — without this entry npm links nothing into apps/admin/node_modules, `npm run dev:admin` does not exist, and the failure looks like a broken script rather than a missing workspace.
_comment_dev: SPLIT 2026-09-01: `dev` keeps meaning "everything", which is now FOUR processes. `dev:front` is the loop most work actually needs, and it deliberately does NOT include admin: three Next servers plus Electron under the 512MB cap is heavy, and most work touches the site and the app. Reach for `dev:console` when the work is on admin — it runs the app beside it, which is what you want, because the two share a Supabase project and the cookie-isolation check (sign in at 3000, open 3003, it must still ask you to sign in) needs both. The ports are not interchangeable: apps/desktop/.env points WEB_URL at 127.0.0.1:3000, so if another app could take that port the desktop would silently talk to it.

scripts.dev: concurrently -n site,web,admin,desktop -c green,cyan,yellow,magenta "npm run dev:site" "npm run dev:web" "npm run dev:admin" "npm run dev:desktop"
scripts.dev:front: concurrently -n site,web -c green,cyan "npm run dev:site" "npm run dev:web"
scripts.dev:console: concurrently -n web,admin -c cyan,yellow "npm run dev:web" "npm run dev:admin"
